newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia end gyrating to a BHP swing on results.
newsitem.headline: Australia end gyrating to a BHP swing on results.

text.p: Australian stocks ended lower on Friday as the share market gyrated within a 20 point band as market heavyweight BHP swung widely after investors assessed the resource giant's first quarter result.
The All Ordinaries index ended 6.3 points lower at 2240.80, but flirted in positive zones throughout the day.
Brokers said investors were mixed about the BHP result, which sent its share price and overall market into a spasm.

"The market has been following BHP up and down all day," one Sydney broker said. The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) reported a 22.8 percent fall in net profit to A$287 million for the three months to August 31, which was within market expectations.
"BHP has certainly been the focus, it was pounded from all quarters after the result, but some fresh buying took place in the afternoon to see it's come back a bit," the broker said.

Shares in BHP swung in a 43 cent range between positive and negative territory all day and had the broader market following in its wake. Brokers said that despite the weak resources, there were still some firm gains in the industrial sector.

"The resources have really dictated this week but don't forget some of the industrials have performed well over the week. The banks have risen quite firmly this week as investors seem to be chasing yield stocks in this market," a broker said.
Chemicals, retail, packaging and insurance sectors were among the few indices to post modest gains today.
However, brokers said metal prices are still likely to command the market direction next week.
The September share price index had a harder fall, 15 points down at 2232 and widening the discount to the underlying index to 8.8 points.
